course.title: Corporate Finance
course.tagline: Build financial judgment with Excel, FactSet, valuation models, and decision-focused practice.
course.studentPromise: Move from reading financial evidence to defending a recommendation a CFO could use.
course.textbookAlignment: Brealey, Myers & Marcus — Fundamentals of Corporate Finance, 11e

learningOutcomes.text: Identify the different types of financial institutions and explain how they enhance capital allocation.
Explain the key financial statements and the information each provides.
Conduct ratio analysis using balance sheets and income statements.
Apply time value of money principles to present value, future value, and yield-to-maturity calculations.
Explain factors affecting the cost of money, interest rates, bond markets, and stock markets.

LO5: Market, bond, risk, and WACC workbooks

tracks.label: Understand the Business
tracks.description: Read markets, financial statements, and performance measures before making a finance recommendation.
tracks.studentQuestion: What is happening inside the business and the market around it?

tracks.label: Value the Cash Flows
tracks.description: Translate timing, risk, and expected cash flows into defensible values for bonds, stocks, and projects.
tracks.studentQuestion: What are these future cash flows worth today?

tracks.label: Recommend the Decision
tracks.description: Connect risk, required returns, and financing choices to a recommendation for management.
tracks.studentQuestion: Which decision creates value, and what evidence supports it?

lessons.title: Course Introduction and Corporate Finance Overview
lessons.summary: Learn how investment, financing, and payout decisions connect to value creation and stakeholder trade-offs.
lessons.prepare: Read the lesson briefing and identify the three decisions made by a financial manager.
lessons.practice: Use the decision framework to separate cash-flow evidence from accounting labels.
lessons.apply: Defend a value-creation recommendation while naming the stakeholder trade-off.
lessons.deliverable: A one-sentence recommendation supported by one cash-flow or risk consideration.

materials.label: View lesson slides
materials.description: Interactive classroom deck for the corporate-finance decision framework.

lessons.title: Financial Institutions, Markets, and Ethics
lessons.summary: Trace how capital moves through institutions and markets, then use market data with an ethical audit trail.
lessons.prepare: Review the difference between primary and secondary markets and confirm FactSet access.
lessons.practice: Calculate and interpret market capitalization using consistent data definitions.
lessons.apply: Explain how one institution reduces a financing friction without overstating the evidence.
lessons.deliverable: A completed market-cap workbook and a two-sentence interpretation.

lessons.summary: Connect the income statement, balance sheet, and cash-flow statement to decision-useful 10-K evidence.
lessons.prepare: Review what each financial statement measures and where the statements connect.
lessons.practice: Trace profit, working capital, and cash through an integrated statement model.
lessons.apply: Use FactSet evidence to explain one operating or financing change at Caterpillar.
lessons.deliverable: A completed CAT worksheet with one evidence-based interpretation.

lessons.summary: Calculate ratios from consistent inputs, decompose the drivers, and interpret performance against a useful benchmark.
lessons.prepare: Review the purpose and denominator of each ratio family.
lessons.practice: Build liquidity, profitability, and leverage ratios from linked statements.
lessons.apply: Explain how operating and financing decisions change performance over time.
lessons.deliverable: A completed ratio model and a driver-based performance recommendation.

lessons.summary: Draw the cash-flow timeline first, then match the Excel function, rate, and period convention to the decision.
lessons.prepare: Review compounding, discounting, sign conventions, and rate-period matching.
lessons.practice: Use PV, FV, and annuity functions with an auditable cash-flow timeline.
lessons.apply: Compare two financing or investment alternatives on the same valuation date.
lessons.deliverable: A formula-audited workbook and a value comparison stated in today’s dollars.

lessons.deliverable: A priced bond, ratio-impact analysis, and CFO recommendation.

lessons.summary: Model incremental cash flows, let NPV lead the decision, and use sensitivity to explain the risk in the recommendation.
lessons.prepare: Review incremental cash flow, sunk costs, terminal effects, and the NPV decision rule.
lessons.practice: Calculate NPV, IRR, PI, and payback using consistent cash-flow timing.
lessons.apply: Recommend a project under uncertainty and identify the assumption that deserves sensitivity testing.
lessons.deliverable: A project model, sensitivity evidence, and written accept-or-reject recommendation.

lessons.title: Risk, Return, and CAPM
lessons.summary: Separate diversifiable and market risk, estimate required return with CAPM, and match the beta to the project.
lessons.prepare: Review holding-period return, volatility, diversification, and beta interpretation.
lessons.practice: Calculate portfolio beta and CAPM required return with auditable formulas.
lessons.apply: Select a project-specific beta and defend the resulting hurdle rate.
lessons.deliverable: A completed CAPM model and a risk-matched project recommendation.

lessons.title: Cost of Capital and WACC
lessons.summary: Estimate current component returns, weight them by market value, and test whether WACC fits the project’s risk.
lessons.prepare: Review CAPM, current debt yield, market-value weights, and the debt tax shield.
lessons.practice: Build each component cost and combine the rows with SUMPRODUCT.
lessons.apply: Decide whether the company WACC is appropriate for a proposed project or valuation.
lessons.deliverable: A formula-audited WACC model and a risk-fit recommendation.
